new_findings.problem: power_report stops with an error for some small standard errors; the power recompute after the Sinkhorn redo could hit it. The root search for the smallest detectable effect starts at 1.0. With scipy 1.17.1, nct.cdf returns NaN at isolated large non-centralities (first at 42.15 for 5 degrees of freedom, 57.24 for 3; 447 of 39,950 tested values on 0.5 to 400 for 5 degrees of freedom), and the solver then stops with 'The function value at x=1.0 is NaN'. It is loud, not silent. It is not 'above about 38' and not for every standard error below 0.026: 7 of 230 (standard error, degrees of freedom) pairs on 0.003 to 0.06 fail (six tasks: 0.0175, 0.0185, 0.0215, 0.022, 0.0225, 0.0235; four families: 0.0165), including the without-sim1 value 0.02355. freeze_a1_grid.py:62 calls power_report on all six blocks (standard error 0.04499, safe). For the planned recompute on the blocks that are not flagged low-signal, the committed pilot blocks give a proxy of 0.02741 (outside the failing values), but the redo changes the inputs.
